2022_279_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.paragraph: Federal awards supplemental information for Troy School District covering the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, presented to the Board of Education as agenda item 8.B. at the October 18, 2022 meeting. The package contains three independent auditor's reports dated October 5, 2022, the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards, a reconciliation of financial statement federal revenue to that schedule, explanatory notes, and the Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs. Federal expenditures for the year totaled $18,847,642, and the audit disclosed no material weaknesses, no significant deficiencies, and no current-year findings, with the district qualifying as a low-risk auditee.
2022_279_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.page:
**What this is**
Federal Awards Supplemental Information for Troy School District, year ended June 30, 2022, a companion to the district's basic financial statements, reviewed by the Board of Education as item 8.B. on October 18, 2022. Contents: independent auditor's reports (pages 1-6), Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (pages 7-10), reconciliation (page 11), notes (page 12), and Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs (page 13).

**Auditor's reports**
Three reports, each dated October 5, 2022. The first opines that the schedule of expenditures of federal awards and the reconciliation are fairly stated in all material respects in relation to the financial statements as a whole; the basic financial statements themselves received an unmodified opinion. The Government Auditing Standards report identified no internal control deficiencies considered material weaknesses and disclosed no reportable instances of noncompliance. The Uniform Guidance report states the district complied, in all material respects, with requirements that could have a direct and material effect on each major federal program, with no material weaknesses in internal control over compliance.

|---|---|---|---|
| Total Educational Stabilization Fund | 13,895,581 | 6,690,111 | 5,017,849 |

Within the Education Stabilization Fund the largest line is COVID-19 ESSER III Funds - Section 11t Equalization (project 213723, ALN 84.425U), award amount 10,707,260 with federal expenditures of 3,760,389 and accrued revenue of 3,760,389 at June 30, 2022. COVID-19 ESSER III Funds - American Rescue Plan (213713) shows award amount 1,895,186 and federal expenditures of 1,895,186; COVID-19 ESSER II Funds - Formula (213712, ALN 84.425D) shows 843,258 in both columns.

**Reconciliation**
Revenue from federal sources as reported on the financial statements, all funds: $21,112,713. Less MDE Child Care Stabilization Fund payments, described as beneficiary payments not subject to single audit: (2,265,071). Federal expenditures per the schedule of expenditures of federal awards: $18,847,642.

**Notes**
Note 1 places the schedule under Title 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Guidance) and states it presents only a selected portion of district operations. Note 2 states expenditures use the same basis of accounting as the basic financial statements, that Coronavirus Relief Fund (ALN 21.027) spending follows U.S. Treasury guidance rather than the Part 200 cost principles, that negative amounts represent prior-year adjustments or credits, and that the district elected not to use the 10 percent de minimis indirect cost rate. Note 3 records use of the Michigan Department of Education NexSys Grant Auditor Report (GAR). Note 4 addresses valuation of noncash assistance.

**Findings and questioned costs**
Unmodified opinion on the financial statements; no material weaknesses or significant deficiencies in internal control over financial reporting; no material noncompliance. For federal awards: no material weaknesses or significant deficiencies in internal control over major programs and no findings required to be reported under 2 CFR 200.516(a). Major programs were the Special Education Cluster (ALNs 84.027, 84.173, 84.027X, 84.173X) and the Education Stabilization Fund (ALNs 84.425, 84.425C, 84.425D, 84.425U), both with unmodified opinions. Type A/type B dollar threshold: $750,000. The district qualified as a low-risk auditee. Section II and Section III each report None for the current year.
2022_279_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.verbose:
Federal Awards Supplemental Information for Troy School District, Michigan, year ended June 30, 2022, delivered to the Board of Education as agenda item 8.B. on the October 18, 2022 agenda. Sections: Report on Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards Required by the Uniform Guidance (page 1); Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting and on Compliance and Other Matters Based on an Audit of Financial Statements Performed in Accordance with Government Auditing Standards (pages 2-3); Report on Compliance for Each Major Federal Program and Report on Internal Control Over Compliance Required by the Uniform Guidance (pages 4-6); Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (pages 7-10); Reconciliation (page 11); Notes (page 12); Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs (page 13).

AUDITOR'S REPORTS. All three carry the date October 5, 2022. The first states the auditor audited the financial statements of the governmental activities, each major fund, and the aggregate remaining fund information as of and for the year ended June 30, 2022, issued a report dated October 5, 2022 containing an unmodified opinion, and performed no procedures on the audited financial statements after that date; in the auditor's opinion the schedule of expenditures of federal awards and the reconciliation are fairly stated in all material respects in relation to the financial statements as a whole. The Government Auditing Standards report defines deficiency, material weakness, and significant deficiency and reports that the audit identified no deficiencies considered material weaknesses and that compliance tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters required to be reported. The Uniform Guidance report opines that the School District complied, in all material respects, with the compliance requirements identified in the OMB Compliance Supplement that could have a direct and material effect on each major federal program for the year ended June 30, 2022, and identifies no material weaknesses in internal control over compliance. Audit standards cited include GAAS, Government Auditing Standards issued by the Comptroller General, and Title 2 CFR Part 200.
